newsitem.title: USA: TWA to acquire a new Boeing 767-300.
newsitem.headline: TWA to acquire a new Boeing 767-300.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc. said Monday it agreed to acquire a new Boeing Co. 767-300 aircraft to be powered by two engines made by the Pratt & Whitney unit of United Technologies Corp.
The aircraft will be acquired through a leasing agreement with International Lease Finance Corp. for undisclosed terms, the airline said.
Delivery is scheduled for February 1998, TWA said.
The aircraft will be the St. Louis-based airline's 15th 767 and its third in the long-range 300 series, it said.
The craft, which will be used on Middle Eastern routes, represents part of a $1 billion upgrade of the airline's 190-plane fleet.
TWA's stock rose 31 cents to $7.44 on the American Stock Exchange at mid-morning. Boeing climbed 94 cents to $56.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
